record.paper_title: Some open problems in the context of skew PBW extensions and semi-graded rings
record.context_brief: Constructive Quillen-Suslin for skew polynomial rings
record.original_question: Let A := K[x_1, . . . , x_n; σ], where K is a field, σ is an automorphism of K of finite order, the variables x_i commute with one another, and x_i r = σ(r) x_i for every r ∈ K and 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n. Can one give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for this ring and, moreover, produce an explicit algorithm that computes a basis for any given finitely generated projective A-module?

evidence.quote: • Give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for A := K[x1, . . . , xn; σ]. Include an algorithm that computes a basis of a given finitely generated projective A-module.

In [21] was solved the previous problem for the case of only one variable, in this particular situation weaker hypotheses can be set, namely, K is a division ring, σ is not necessarily of finite order and a non trivial σ-derivation δ of K can be added.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and let $\sigma$ be an automorphism of $K$ of finite order. Consider the iterated skew polynomial ring
$$A := K[x_1, \ldots, x_n; \sigma],$$
defined as the $K$-algebra generated by $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ subject to the relations
- $x_i x_j = x_j x_i$ for all $1 \le i, j \le n$, and
- $x_i r = \sigma(r) x_i$ for every $r \in K$ and every $1 \le i \le n$.

It is known (a noncommutative analogue of the Quillen–Suslin theorem) that every finitely generated projective left $A$-module is free. The task is the following:

Provide a matrix-constructive proof of this fact. More precisely, give an explicit algorithm which, on input a finitely generated projective left $A$-module $M$ (presented, e.g., by an idempotent matrix over $A$ or by generators and relations), outputs a finite free basis of $M$ as a left $A$-module, together with the explicit unimodular transformation matrices over $A$ realizing the isomorphism $M \cong A^r$.
artifact.status_search_result: A constructive/algorithmic Quillen–Suslin theorem is known for the commutative polynomial ring case and for the one-variable skew polynomial case (under weaker hypotheses, allowing K a division ring, σ of arbitrary order, plus a σ-derivation). For the multivariate skew polynomial ring K[x_1,…,x_n;σ] with σ of finite order and commuting variables, no matrix-constructive proof or explicit basis-computing algorithm appears in the literature; the problem is listed among open problems on skew PBW extensions.

status_evidence.title: An Algorithmic Proof of Suslin's Stability Theorem for Polynomial Rings
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic proof of Suslin's stability theorem; factorization of polynomial matrices into elementary ones using Gröbner bases.
status_evidence.claim: Constructive algorithms exist in the commutative polynomial setting, not in the skew multivariate setting addressed here.

status_evidence.title: Univariate skew polynomial rings (SageMath)
status_evidence.snippet: Specialized class SkewPolynomialRing_finite_order for skew polynomial rings with automorphism of finite order; covers the univariate case.
status_evidence.claim: Effective tools exist for the one-variable skew case, in line with the noted prior solution for n=1.
